name: Performance: VertiPaq, query plans, aggregations, incremental refresh

why.matters: Slow reports stop being used, and a model that is too big costs real capacity money every hour.
why.failure: An executive page takes 18 seconds every Monday because one measure iterates the whole fact table per cell.
why.use: Measure first: Performance Analyzer, DAX query view and Server Timings tell you whether the time is in visuals, the formula engine or the storage engine.
why.avoid: Optimising without a baseline. Every change needs a before and after number.

verified.context: Performance Analyzer, DAX query view, incremental refresh docs, Sept 2026

asg.t: Make a big fact and measure it
steps: In Power Query, reference FactSales and cross-join it with a 1,000-row list (List.Numbers) to get 100,000 rows; add a random offset to dates. Name it FactSalesBig.
Open DAX Studio → Advanced → View Metrics (VertiPaq Analyzer). Record total model size and the top 3 columns by size.
Change SalesKey to not loaded (remove it), and change UnitPrice from Decimal to Fixed Decimal. Re-run metrics. Record the size difference.
Split OrderDate/ShipDate into Date only (remove time). Record again.
asg.exp: A table with before/after sizes. The high-cardinality key column dominates size; removing it saves the most.

steps: Write the slow version: Customers Over 500 Slow = COUNTROWS(FILTER(FactSalesBig, [Net Sales] > 500)).
In DAX Studio, Server Timings on, run a matrix query using it. Record FE ms, SE ms, number of SE queries, and whether CallbackDataID appears.
Rewrite once more with SUMMARIZE + a filter on a pre-computed column; compare.
asg.exp: Version 1 shows one SE query per row or a CallbackDataID; version 2 is 10× fewer SE queries.

steps: Create AggSalesMonthCat in Power Query: group FactSalesBig by YearMonth, Category, RegionKey with Sum Quantity, Sum Amount, Count rows.
Set FactSalesBig to DirectQuery (or keep Import and just practise the mapping), AggSalesMonthCat to Import. Manage aggregations: map each column.
In DAX Studio, run a query by Category and check the "Aggregation hit" in the query plan event; then run by ProductName and confirm it misses.
asg.exp: One query hits the agg (Category grain), one misses (Product grain).

asg.ds: FactSalesBig via SQL or a partitioned CSV folder
steps: RangeStart/RangeEnd parameters; filter step that folds.
Incremental refresh policy: archive 2 years, refresh 3 days, detect data changes on a ModifiedDate column if you have one.
Publish, refresh, then in SSMS or Tabular Editor via XMLA endpoint (needs capacity/PPU) look at the partitions created.
Simulate a late-arriving fact and confirm it is not picked up outside the refresh window. Then fix with a longer window.
asg.exp: Partition list shows year, quarter, month and day partitions.

steps: Write Conversion Rate = DIVIDE([Sessions With Purchase], DISTINCTCOUNT(WebEvents[SessionID])).

Write Avg Session Minutes two ways: (a) AVERAGEX(VALUES(SessionID), DATEDIFF(CALCULATE(MIN(EventTime)), CALCULATE(MAX(EventTime)), MINUTE)) and (b) with a calculated column SessionStart via EARLIER, then a measure. Compare the query plan cost and model size.
asg.exp: You can articulate when to pay the cost at refresh (column) versus at query (measure).

int.q: How does VertiPaq compress data, and what is the single biggest lever?
int.a: Dictionary encoding per column plus run-length encoding on the sorted values. Cardinality is the lever: fewer distinct values → smaller dictionary and longer runs. So remove high-cardinality columns, round decimals, split datetime into date and time.

int.q: Formula engine vs storage engine: what runs where?
int.a: SE (VertiPaq) executes simple scans, filters and aggregations in parallel and is fast. FE is single-threaded and handles everything the SE cannot: iterators calling measures, complex conditions, TOPN over measures. Optimising = pushing work from FE to SE.

int.q: What is a CallbackDataID and why is it bad?
int.a: The SE calling back into the FE per row because an expression inside an iterator cannot be executed by SE (e.g. IF, DIVIDE with a measure). It serialises the scan and defeats the SE cache.

int.q: Aggregations: when do they not help?
int.a: When the query grain is finer than the agg table, when a measure uses DISTINCTCOUNT (needs the detail unless you build a count-distinct agg with GroupBy), or when RLS filters columns not in the agg table.

int.q: Incremental refresh: what happens on the first refresh after publishing, and how do you avoid a timeout?
int.a: The first refresh loads all historical partitions and can time out. Publish the model with no partitions loaded, then refresh partitions in batches via XMLA (Tabular Editor / SSMS), or use bootstrap "Apply refresh policy" without data first.

int.q: Give three model-level performance rules you enforce in code review.
int.a: No calculated columns on facts unless justified, no bi-directional relationships without a written reason, integer keys not text, dates without time, measures over iterators over facts, hide and remove unused columns, Fixed Decimal for currency.

ass.q: Which change reduces model size most?
o: Remove a unique integer key column from a 100k-row fact
ass.why: Unique keys have a dictionary as large as the table.

o: First is far more expensive due to per-row context transition
ass.why: Iterating 100k fact rows with a measure creates 100k context transitions.

ass.q: Produce a VertiPaq Analyzer before/after table for FactSalesBig with at least three optimisations and the % reduction of each.
ass.hint: Key removal, Fixed Decimal, date/time split, removing unused columns.

ass.q: Detect data changes in incremental refresh requires:
o: A datetime column such as LastModified that folds
ass.why: The policy compares MAX(LastModified) per partition.
